title: Why he played chords instead of picking, and switching to banjo
summary: Vincent says he was told picking was too light for the band, so he played chords. He moved from guitar to banjo, learning from Professor Boeese.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Ask him in the old days, when he first started picking a heart, did he play chords or single string or both?

Listen, he said when you first started playing, did you get a heart and pick, or just play chords all the time? Chords. Chords. You never picked? I tried. I used to pick, but they told me picking was too light for the band. They told me don't pick, you make chords. You see, I first learned on the mountain then. That was what made me just pick when I got out of the guitar. But I used to pick, and they told me they couldn't hear me. Don't pick, make chords. And that's why I got out of picking. Then I forgot how to pick, you know, when the picking come back. I should have got an electricity guitar. Now that's why they probably picked, you see. I never did own an electricity guitar. So I got off the guitar and went on a banjo. You know, it's like a professor Boeese, huh?
Well, he's the one who learned me how to pick banjo, you see. When I was bad, I used to run across him all the time, you know. He's got a ban now, you know.
